  * Improved label positioning while moving diagram elements.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for initial layouts, automatic cuts, configuration behavior, and layout resets.

clientPayload.reply_to_text:
Researched this in the actual svsch code (cloned + read the parser/IR/renderer). Findings:

**Today:** `(a|b)&c` and `a&b&c&d` already collapse into ONE opaque `comb` box (textExtractor.ts / expressions.inc `getOrPromoteExpr`) — no gate structure at all, just a box listing every leaf signal as an input. So you're not choosing between "gate node" and "nothing," it's "gate node" vs "undifferentiated blob."

**Adding real AND/OR/XOR/NAND/NOR/XNOR/NOT gate nodes is a clean, localized change:**
- IR: `DiagramNodeKind` already has `alu`/`inverter`/`comb` — adding `gate` w/ n-ary ports is one more union member, no new concept (ir/types.ts).
- Rendering precedent already exists 3x over: NOT is a literal hand-drawn triangle+bubble glyph (InverterNodeSvg.tsx) using the same pattern mux/alu use (trapezoid via nodeSizing.ts). Gate shapes (AND D-shape, OR curved-back, XOR double-curve) slot into the same `HdlNode.tsx` kind-dispatch.
- Width is already tracked per-operand, so flattening can be verified lossless before collapsing.

**Your associativity worry — verdict: doesn't apply to logic gates, DOES apply to arithmetic, and the codebase already half-knows this:**
- `&`/`|`/`^` are genuinely one library cell in real synthesis up to fan-in limits — no carry chain, no cascade-vs-tree tradeoff exists for a pure bitwise gate. Collapsing `a&b&c&d` → one 4-input AND is honest, not an aggressive assumption.
- `+`/`-` are the opposite: real adders ARE carry chains, cascade-vs-balanced-tree is a genuine timing/area tradeoff. The code's own `promoteAluExpr` already refuses to chain nested `+`/`-` into one ALU node for exactly this reason — it just currently gives up and shows an undifferentiated blob instead of a real cascade/tree. If gate work happens, arithmetic should go the OPPOSITE direction: show real 2-input adder chains matching source structure, not flatten.
- Hard rule either way: never flatten ACROSS operator types. `(a|b)&c` must stay OR-feeding-AND, never merged — the existing `isAluOperation` operand-type check already has the right instinct for this.
- No existing fan-in cap or gate-library convention anywhere in the repo — that's a fresh design call (e.g. cap visual gates at 4-6 inputs and cascade beyond that for realism, or always show true count).
- Bonus finding: reduction ops (`&expr`, `|expr`, `^expr`) aren't handled as a distinct kind anywhere yet — same flattening logic could cover them (inputs = bit-slices of one bus instead of distinct signals), worth folding into the same design.

Want me to file this as a scoping issue (gate nodes: AND/OR/XOR/NAND/NOR/XNOR/NOT + n-ary flattening, explicitly scoped to bitwise/logical ops only, arithmetic left alone or improved separately)?

issue.body:
$Gate the array address-mux insertion with the same per-array existence check used for the register node.\n\nAdds a regression covering reset-loop and indexed writes to the same array.\n\nFixes #101

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed duplicate address-mux generation for multiple indexed writes to the same array.
  * Preserved distinct array index paths and correct write priority.
  * Improved handling of full-array reset loops, including non-zero reset values.
  * Ensured reset and array write connections remain complete and correctly wired.

* **Tests**
  * Added regression and visual coverage for chained address muxes, repeated indexed writes, full-array resets, and partial-range reset handling.
